pages._note: Service catalogue as a declarative type:index page (pipelinq-views-to-declarative-r2). price→EUR currency, durationMinutes→duration format, status→badge, bookableOnline→boolean. 'New service' navigates to the bespoke ServiceDetail create form (id:'new'); row open navigates to ServiceDetail. ServiceDetail stays custom (multiStep sub-table editor + policy cards + cache-invalidation hook).
pages.title: Services
Service
pages._note: Uses CnDetailPage/CnDetailCard, but a type:detail page cannot carry the SIDE EFFECT this one owes: every save calls invalidateAvailability, because changing a service's duration or required skills invalidates the cached booking-availability windows computed from it. Stale windows would offer slots that can no longer be honoured. It also derives display-only labels (formatDuration, formatCurrency, requiredSkillsLabel) that are not schema properties.

Resource catalogue (staff/room/equipment) as a declarative type:index page (pipelinq-views-to-declarative-r2): the literal navigate params primitive now expresses 'New resource' → ResourceDetail id:'new'. type→badge, bookable→boolean, status→badge. ResourceDetail stays custom (workingHours grid + vacation list + cache invalidation).
pages.title: Resources
Resource
pages._note: Same reason as ServiceDetail: a type:detail page cannot own the post-save invalidateAvailability side effect, and a resource's skills or working hours changing must expire the cached availability windows or the booking flow will offer slots this resource can no longer serve. It additionally holds a live useObjectSubscription so a concurrently edited resource updates in place, which declarative detail pages do not do.

Customer appointment ledger as a declarative type:index page (pipelinq-views-to-declarative-r1). View-only — admins create bookings through the public portal flow, never from this list — so the row click is the only action and navigates to the bespoke BookingDetail (reschedule/cancel/act), which stays custom.
pages.title: Bookings

pages._note: Booking record as a declarative type:detail page (pipelinq-pos-mdm-detail-declarative). The booking's flat identity fields (status / source / startAt / endAt / depositAmount / notes / …) auto-render in the body via CnObjectDataWidget. Everything the auto-body + relatedCollections cannot express lives in one kind:'section' bodyWidget (BookingDetailSection, after-data): the six TIME-WINDOW-gated admin actions, the inline notes/internalNotes editor, the resourceAssignments + statusHistory ARRAY-on-object tables (with cross-schema resource id->name resolution), the computed Timeline, and the Service/Customer name resolution. KEPT-AS-NOTE: lifecycleActions is NOT wired even though booking HAS an x-openregister-lifecycle — the real transitions POST to bespoke /api/bookings/{id}/{action} endpoints in BookingService with side-effects (confirmation/reminder emails, no-show fees) and TIME-WINDOW gating, and Reschedule CREATES A NEW booking UUID and navigates to it; OR's /transition would only flip status and bypass those side-effects. So the actions stay inside the section. Missing primitive: a declarative action that POSTs to a host-app endpoint (not OR /transition) with time-window gating + a 'returns a new object id, navigate to it' reload mode.
pages.title: Booking

config._note: Booking archetype (bespoke-detail-pages). An appointment booking is a scheduled service slot, so the body opens with a deposit KPI stat then the booking fields (status, source, startAt/endAt, customerId, serviceId, depositAmount, confirmation/reminder timestamps, cancellationReason) 8-wide and the related graph (service, resource, customer, previousBookingId reschedule chain) 4-wide, with Documents full-width for any signed intake / deposit receipt. IMPORTANT: no calendar body widget or tab — although a booking is time-bound, the booking schema declares NO calendar linkedType, and per the hard rule comms/scheduling leaves only appear when the schema declares them; the real schedule + the six TIME-WINDOW-gated admin actions, the resourceAssignments/statusHistory arrays-on-object and the computed Timeline all stay in the PRESERVED BookingDetailSection bodyWidget (after-data), whose note explains why lifecycleActions cannot be wired (bespoke endpoints, side-effects, reschedule mints a new UUID).
